first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, making simplification the most directly aligned intervention. I will verify the prior onboarding and signup experiments because their relevance to sustainable qualified revenue, including any impact from reduced qualification data, is not established. A small guarded test limits downstream risk while measuring activation, qualified pipeline, retention, and revenue quality.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, guarded experiment shortening onboarding, prioritizing self-serve accounts where completion and activation are currently declining. The verified result shows a 13% completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention, making this the strongest path to sustainable qualified revenue. Signup simplification also improved SMB activation and qualified revenue, but its 1% retention decline and lack of replication beyond SMB warrant segment-specific analysis rather than a broad rollout. Measure activation, completion, time-to-value, retention, qualified revenue, and lead quality.

final2.rationale: Launch a tightly targeted, time-limited promotional pricing test for demonstrably price-sensitive SMB accounts facing churn, with eligibility and margin guardrails. The inherited evidence indicates promotional pricing can lift SMB acquisition and revenue, while signup simplification confirms this segment’s responsiveness but does not address the immediate competitive price shock. Because pricing effects on long-term retention, discount dependence, and qualified revenue have not been verified this cycle, measure incremental retention, gross-margin-adjusted revenue, qualified conversion, and churn against a holdout rather than broadly matching the competitor.
